rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘as long as the heavens and earth endure’ signifies perpetuity as a proverbial expression; the familiar heavens and earth will perish, or it can mean the heavens and earth of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ما دامت السماوات والأرض } التأييد لأنه جرى مجرى المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may qualify the times covered by ‘as long as,’ thereby also excluding some inhabitants by implication; this fits the usual nonrational sense of ما.
rows.anchor: استثناء من الأزمان التي عمها الظرف في قوله : { ما دامت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception may qualify the pronoun ‘abiding’; ما often refers to rational beings, as in ‘whatever women are lawful to you.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استثناء من ضمير { خالدين } لأن { ما } تطلق على العاقل كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first exception allows different terms in Hell: sinful monotheists may be punished and then forgiven, while polytheists and unbelievers remain there forever.
rows.anchor: فأما الأول منهما فالمقصود أن أهل النار مراتب في طول المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is an explanatory resumption prompted by the exception’s ambiguity, which raises the question of whom it excludes or why abiding is not universal; it teaches entrusting the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } استئناف بياني ناشىء عن الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is the first period of the Resurrection, when unrepentant sinful believers enter punishment until God forgives them, with or without intercession.
rows.anchor: وأما الاستثناء الثاني الواقع في جانب { الذين سعدوا } فيحتمل معنيين

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas’s sound hadith describes people entering Hell until they become like charcoal, then being brought out and admitted to Paradise as the ‘Jahannamiyyun.’
rows.anchor: في الصحيح من حديث أنس : ( يدخل ناس جنم حتى إذا صاروا كالحممة أخرجوا وأدخلوا الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception warns against imagining that anyone has a claim to bliss binding on God; Paradise is a manifestation of divine grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقصد منه التحذير من توهم استحقاق أحد ذلك النعيم حقا على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A will-conditioned exception does not mean God will enact it; it means only that the exception would occur if He willed it. His promises show He will not remove Paradise’s people.
rows.anchor: وليس يلزم من الاستثناء المعلق على المشيئة وقوع المشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once admitted to Paradise, its people abide forever and their bliss never ends; this is the meaning of the gift that is not cut off.
rows.anchor: فهم إذا أدخلوا الجنة كانوا خالدين فيها فلا ينقطع عنهم نعيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-majdhudh means ‘cut off.’
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قوله : { عطاء غير مجذوذ } . والمجذوذ : المقطوع .

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read saʿidu with fatḥa on the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { سعدوا } بفتح السين

rows.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم، وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use ḍamma on the sīn, treating the verb as passive though its base is intransitive: it means ‘made happy.’
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف بضم السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading is explained by treating an intransitive verb as transitive in the sense of someone being made to acquire a quality, as in جن فلان.
rows.anchor: على معاملة القاصر معاملة المتعدي في معنى فعل به ما صيره صاحب ذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that سعد is transitive in the Hudhayl and Tamim dialects, meaning ‘God made him happy.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : سعد متعد في لغة هذيل وتميم ، يقولون : سعده الله بمعنى أسعده .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis derives the form from أُسعدوا by dropping the augmenting hamza, as in مجنوب and مسعود.
rows.anchor: وخرج أيضا على أن أصله أسعدوا ، فحذف همز الزيادة كما قالوا مجنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qurun means nations or communities; Ibn ʿAshūr refers to his discussion at the beginning of al-Anʿam.
rows.anchor: والقرون : الأمم . وتقدم في أول الأنعام .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyya means virtue and goodness; calling virtue a ‘remainder’ became a conventional metaphor because people do not discard what is precious.
rows.anchor: والبقية : الفضل والخير . وأطلق على الفضل البقية كناية غلبت

rows.speaker: رويَشد بن كثير الطائي
rows.claim: The poet’s use of بقيتكم (‘your remainder’) illustrates the term for a community’s eminent, virtuous people; a proverb similarly speaks of ‘remnants’ among men.
rows.anchor: قال رويشد بن كثير الطائي : إن تذنبوا ثم تأتيني بقيتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant are followers of messengers who possess virtue, piety, and knowledge of the revealed law, not the messengers themselves; they warn their communities against corruption.
rows.anchor: والمعنى هنا : أولو فضل ودين وعلم بالشريعة ، فليس المراد الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption includes sins and disrupted social conditions. Prohibition restrains reckless sin and repairs conditions, averting the decline that befell the Israelites when no one admonished them.
rows.anchor: والفساد : المعاصي واختلاف الأحوال ، فنهيهم يردعهم عن الاستهتار في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse praises the Prophet’s Companions: some called Quraysh to faith until they believed; among other peoples they called people to faith and uprightness and taught religion.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تنويه بأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنهم أولو بقية من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ‘before you’ hints at the glad tiding that Muslims will not be like those prior communities.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { من القرون من قبلكم } إشارة إلى البشارة بأن المسلمين لا يكونون كذلك

rows.speaker: ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn Jammāz from Abū Jaʿfar reads biqya with kasra on bāʾ, a still qāf, and a light yāʾ; Ibn ʿAshūr calls it a dialect form absent from lexicons, perhaps suggesting dignified bearing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر ( بقية ) بكسر الباء الموحدة وسكون القاف وتخفيف التحتية فهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Except a few’ is a detached exception from ‘people of virtue,’ and by implication from the former nations; its accusative marks disconnection, while a connected exception would be nominative by substitution.
rows.anchor: و { إلا قليلا } استثناء منقطع من { أولوا بقية } وهو يستتبع الاستثناء من القرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detached exception corrects a possible implication that every pre-Muslim nation lacked people of virtue: a few did have them, while the verse censures the many who lacked them.
rows.anchor: ولكن لما كان معنى التحضيض قد يوهم أن جميع القرون التي كانت قبل المسلمين قد عدموا أولي بقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory, clarifying that the few whom God saved from those nations were the people who forbade corruption, followers of the messengers.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { ممن أنجينا } بيانية ، بيان للقليل لأن الذين أنجاهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admonition led to salvation as the cause of repentance: they stopped sinning and were thereby saved from the Fire, which no one can repel.
rows.anchor: وفي البيان إشارة إلى أن نهيهم عن الفساد هو سبب إنجاء تلك القرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits an idea to be supplied: they repented and abandoned corruption on earth, so they escaped the Fire.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله : { ممن أنجينا منهم } على أن في الكلام إيجاز حذفف تقديره : فكانوا يتوبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause makes explicit the implication of the exception: most neither forbade corruption nor desisted, and followed their indulgence, much as 2:34 spells out the implication of its exception.
rows.anchor: وجملة { واتبع الذين ظلموا } معطوفة على ما أفاده الاستثناء من وجود قليل ينهون عن الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage admonishes sinful Muslims too, since they are never entirely free of wronging themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية عبرة وموعظة للعصاة من المسلمين لأنهم لا يخلون من ظلم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following what they were indulged in means devoting themselves to it and pursuing it as a follower pursues the one followed.
rows.anchor: واتباع ما أترفوا فيه هو الانقطاع له والإقبال عليه إقبال المتبع على متبوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were granted luxury, abundance, and ease by God, but failed to thank Him for it.
rows.anchor: وأترفوا : أعطوا الترف ، وهو السعة والنعيم الذي سهله الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were criminals in their pursuit of luxury because they were ungrateful; enjoying luxury with gratitude would not be exclusive devotion to it.
rows.anchor: و { كانوا مجرمين } أي في اتباع الترف فلم يكونوا شاكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further ellipsis supplies that the fate of criminals became due upon them, preparing for the next verse’s statement that God would not destroy towns unjustly.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز حذف آخر ، والتقدير : فحق عليهم هلاك المجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge of each pregnancy exemplifies hidden particulars no creature then knows and no idol can be consulted about; the particular example establishes the universal claim.
rows.anchor: وذكر من معلومات الله ما لا نزاع في أنه لا يعلمه أحد من الخلق يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What every female carries includes human and animal embryos; the verse uses ‘carry’ rather than ‘conceive’ because conception language is specific to women.
rows.anchor: فما تحمل كل أنثى هي أجنة الإنسان والحيوان . ولذلك جيء بفعل الحمل دون الحبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is a relative pronoun, and its generality covers each fetus’s sex, completeness or deficiency, beauty or ugliness, height or shortness, and color.
rows.anchor: وما } موصولة ، وعمومها يقتضي علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes decrease as conception: the womb’s ‘decrease’ is the cessation of menstruation, while increase is menstrual flow.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه كناية عن العلوق لأن غيض الرحم انحباس دم الحيض عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, decrease is a metaphor for absence of multiple embryos and increase means plurality: a womb may contain one embryo or several in humans or animals.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الغيض مستعارا لعدم التعدد . والازدياد : التعدد أي ما يكون في الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with God’s knowledge of pregnancies; ‘thing’ means an object of knowledge. One parse makes ‘with Him’ the predicate and ‘in due measure’ circumstantial; another makes the measure phrase the predicate.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وكل شيء عنده بمقدار } معطوفة على جملة { يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miqdār is a mimī verbal noun, indicated by the preposition bi, meaning estimation, fixing, and exact determination; God knows every thing in full detail without vagueness.
rows.anchor: والمقدار : مصدر ميمي بقرينة الباء ، أي بتقدير ، ومعناه : التحديد والضبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes non-Muslim philosophers who said the Necessary Existent knows universals but not particulars to avoid knowledge of contingent events; theologians have decisively disproved their doctrine.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا رد على الفلاسفة غير المسلمين القائلين أن واجب الوجود يعلم الكليات ولا يعلم الجزئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Knower of the unseen and the visible’ sums up the universal reach of knowledge over hidden and manifest things, the two classes of existent things; the unseen was mentioned at the start of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وجملة { عالم الغيب والشهادة } تذييل وفذلكة لتعميم العلم بالخفيات والظواهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is an explanatory resumption and consequence of God’s comprehensive knowledge of hidden and manifest things.
rows.anchor: موقع هذه الجملة استئناف بياني لأن مضمونها بمنزلة النتيجة لعموم علم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts from third-person reference to direct address to teach both believers and unbelievers, while implicitly threatening polytheists conspiring against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الغيبة المتبعة في الضمائر فيما تقدم إلى الخطاب هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ means equal and is used between two or more things; Arabic usage keeps it in one form, as in ‘they are equal’ and ‘you are equal in it.’
rows.anchor: و { سواء } اسم بمعنى مستو . وإنما يقع معناه بين شيئين فصاعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes sawāʾ the subject and man the subject-like element filling the predicate slot; alternatively sawāʾ is a fronted predicate, man the delayed subject, and minkum a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وموقع سواء هنا موقع المبتدأ . و { من أسر القول } فاعل سد مسد الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikhfāʾ here means concealment; the sīn and tāʾ intensify the action, as in istajāba.
rows.anchor: والاستخفاء : هنا الخفاء ، فالسين والتاء للمبالغة في الفعل مثل استجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib is an active participle from saraba, to go along a road or path; this verb is derived from a concrete noun.
rows.anchor: والسارب : اسم فاعل من سرب إذا ذهب في السرب بفتح السين وسكون الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concealment is paired with night because it is the more hidden state, and movement with day because it is more visible; both kinds are equally known to God.
rows.anchor: وذكر الاستخفاء مع الليل لكونه أشد خفاء ، وذكر السروب مع النهار لكونه أشد ظهورا

words: وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍۭ بِٱلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌۢ بِٱلنَّهَارِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw joining the relative expressions marks division among the categories and therefore functions like ‘or.’
rows.anchor: والواو التي عطفت أسماء الموصول على الموصول الأول للتقسيم فهي بمعنى { أو }

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of revelation is to guide people: God did not leave them astray. The guided follow His direction; those who stray choose desire over guidance’s evidence, and God’s commands serve wisdom and interests of varying importance.
rows.anchor: وتعليل الإنزال بالإخراج من الظلمات دل على أن الهداية هي مراد الله تعالى من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Bringing out’ is a metaphor for moving people from one state to another, with transition likened to exit and the act of moving likened to bringing out.
rows.anchor: شبه الانتقال بالخروج فشبه النقل بالإخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness and light metaphorically represent disbelief and faith: disbelief confuses, while faith guides to truth. The hearer may picture a bewildered person emerging from darkness into a bright place.
rows.anchor: استعارة للكفر والإيمان ، لأن الكفر يجعل صاحبه في حيرة فهو كالظلمة في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘darknesses’ and singular ‘light’ were explained at the beginning of al-Anʿam.
rows.anchor: تقدم في أول سورة الأنعام ( 1 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is causal. Permission is a command to act that depends on the commander’s consent; here it is God’s authorization of the Messenger’s mission, as in the statement that every messenger is sent to be obeyed by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: للسببية ، والإذن : الأمر بفعل يتوقف على رضى الآمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sending is for people’s benefit, permission is attributed to their Lord, who manages their interests.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإرسال لمصلحتهم أضيف الإذن إلى وصف الرب المضاف إلى ضمير الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘To the path’ is apposition to ‘the light’; the repeated preposition elaborates the appositive and gives it emphasis, as in the cited wording from al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: إلى صراط العزيز الحميد ( سورة إبراهيم : 1 ) بدل من النور } بإعادة الجار للمبدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor of the path for true religion suits the imagery of bringing people from darkness into light and its implied comparison.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة الصراط المستعار للدين الحق ، لاستعارة الإخراج والظلمات والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These attributes best suit the context: the unconquerable God’s revealed Book proves His purpose right, overcomes opponents, and establishes the proof against them.
rows.anchor: لأن العزيز الذي لا يغلب . وإنزال الكتاب برهان على أحقية ما أراده الله من الناس

words: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: نافع، وابن عامر، وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers put the name Allah in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: ‘He—the Mighty, Praiseworthy—is God, to whom belongs all in the heavens and earth.’
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر برفع اسم الجلالة على أنه خبر عن مبتدإ محذوف .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted subject follows a familiar Arabic usage: after describing someone, speakers move to a more consequential predicate, reinforcing the purpose; al-Sakkākī calls this omission to follow usage. The cited couplets by Ibrāhīm al-Ṣūlī exemplify the omitted ‘he’ before فتى.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحذف جار على حذف المسند إليه المسمى عند علماء المعاني تبعا للسكاكي بالحذف لمتابعة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: الباقون إلا رويسا عن يعقوب
rows.claim: The remaining readers apart from Ruways from Yaʿqūb read Allah in the genitive as an appositive to ‘the Mighty, Praiseworthy’; this is an Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الباقون إلا رويسا عن يعقوب بالجر على البدلية من { العزيز الحميد }

rows.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Ruways from Yaʿqūb reads the name in the nominative when pausing after al-Ḥamīd and beginning with Allah, but in the genitive when linking the words.
rows.anchor: وقرأه رويس عن يعقوب - بالرفع - إذا وقف على قوله ' الحميد '

words: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings reach the same point: Allah is more worthy of mention after the prior attributes, though the nominative is more emphatic. The relative clause magnifies Him rather than identifying Him, since the audience already knows Him as owner of all beings.
rows.anchor: ومآل القراءتين واحد وكلتا الطريقتين تفيد أن المنتقل إليه أجدر بالذكر عقب ما تقدمه

words: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause indirectly rebukes idolaters: the path of anything besides God cannot reach its destination because its objects are deficient, and their idols do not own the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن صراط غير الله من طرق آلهتهم ليس بواصل إلى المقصود لنقصان ذويه

words: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path belonging to God, who owns all things, implicitly criticizes polytheists for following another path; the discourse turns to threaten them with punishment for associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: لما أفاد قوله : { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض } تعريضا بالمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Woe to the disbelievers’ is a curse-like prayer spoken in anger and censure, like wayḥak, coordinated as a performative utterance with the preceding report.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وويل للكافرين } إنشاء دعاء عليهم في مقام الغضب والذم ، مثل قولهم : ويحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is a verbal noun without a known verb, meaning destruction or a similarly dire condition; it is treated as a noun of action, accusative as an absolute object or nominative for constancy.
rows.anchor: مصدر لا يعرف له فعل ، ومعناه الهلاك وما يقرب منه من سوء الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl also appears as ويل لك, ويلك, or يا ويلك; its cause follows with min, indicating destruction arising from the severe punishment of Hell.
rows.anchor: وقد يذكر بعد هذا التركيب سببه فيؤتى به مجرورا بحرف { من } الابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known disbelievers are the polytheists who did not leave darkness for light, follow God’s path, or benefit from the revealed Book.
rows.anchor: والكافرون هم المعهودون وهم الذين لم يخرجوا من الظلمات إلى النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastahibbūna means ‘love,’ with sīn and tāʾ intensifying the sense. Context adds ‘prefer’: they love worldly good instead of afterlife good, where they face suffering, so the verb takes a second object with ʿalā.
rows.anchor: ويستحبون } بمعنى يحبون ، فالسين والتاء للتأكيد مثل استقدم واستأخر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage resumes the argument against taking rivals alongside God, after the intervening command about believers’ prayer. Listing blessings exposes ingratitude, contrasts it with gratitude, and increases the grateful in thankfulness; the main target is the pagan Arabs, as the following Abraham prayer signals.
rows.anchor: استئناف واقع موقع الاستدلال على ما تضمنته جملة { وجعلوا لله أندادا } الآية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are general, tangible blessings that cannot reasonably be denied; people need reminding that God is their giver and creator.
rows.anchor: فجيء في هذه الآية بنعم عامة مشهودة محسوسة لا يستطاع إنكارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins with the Creator’s name because identifying Him is the chief purpose; the relative clause states what is already accepted, since the polytheists did not claim idols created anything.
rows.anchor: وافتتح الكلام باسم الموجد لأن تعيينه هو الغرض الأهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation proves the Creator’s divinity and prepares for the listed blessings: rain and fruit, seas and rivers, sun and moon, and night and day. These blessings were explained in earlier verses.
rows.anchor: فخلق السماوات والأرض دليل على إلهية خالقهما وتمهيد للنعم المودعة فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq means sustenance or food.
rows.anchor: والرزق القوت . والتسخير : حقيقته التذليل والتطويع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taskhīr literally means subduing and making compliant; figuratively, it makes something available for another’s use and control. Ibn ʿAshūr refers to 7:54.
rows.anchor: والتسخير : حقيقته التذليل والتطويع ، وهو مجاز في جعل الشيء قابلا لتصرف غيره فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘to sail in the sea’ gives the purpose for which the ships were made subject to human use.
rows.anchor: البحر } هو علة تسخير صنعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to 14:28: Meccans failed to thank God for blessings granted through answering Abraham’s prayer, abandoned their righteous forebears’ example for misguided ancestors, and repaid Abraham’s prayer with ingratitude.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمة الله كفرا ( إبراهيم : 28 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it coordinates with the account of God creating the heavens and earth: the discourse moves from general blessings, which include Mecca, to blessings specific to its people, praising Abraham and alluding to his polytheist descendants.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون معطوفة على جملة الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض } بأن انتقل من ذكر النعم العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is an accusative time noun governed by an omitted common verb, estimated as ‘remember when’; it heightens wonder at the polytheists as in 14:28 and recalls the same lesson.
rows.anchor: اسم زمان ماض منصوب على المفعولية لفعل محذوف شائع الحذف في أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is a vocative with the calling particle omitted; its original form is rabbī, with the first-person yāʾ commonly dropped for lightness in vocatives.
rows.anchor: و { رب } منادى محذوف منه حرف النداء . وأصله ( ربي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-balad means a specified tract of land and can also mean a town; the definite article marks a known place, and al-balad apposes the demonstrative.
rows.anchor: والبلد : المكان المعين من الأرض ، ويطلق على القرية . والتعريف في { البلد } تعريف العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer leaves the town unnamed, either to create suspense before identifying it as the place near the Sacred House, or because Arabs knew it meant Mecca. This matches 2:126: here Abraham asks this city to be safe; there he asks that the indicated place become one of the safe cities.
rows.anchor: وحكاية دعائه بدون بيان البلد إبهام يرد بعده البيان بقوله : { عند بيتك المحرم ( سورة إبراهيم : 37 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘I have settled some of my descendants’ begins a new prayer. Its opening invocation intensifies supplication and links the invocation-led clauses as like instances.
rows.anchor: جملة { إني أسكنت من ذريتي } مستأنفة لابتداء دعاء آخر . وافتتحت بالنداء لزيادة التضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation says ‘our Lord’ rather than the earlier ‘my Lord’ because Abraham’s prayer concerns both himself and his sons; Ishmael may be present, as the joint prayer in 2:127 suggests.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الرب هنا إلى ضمير الجمع خلافا لسابقيه لأن الدعاء الذي افتتح به فيه حظ للداعي ولأبنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min means ‘some of’; the descendant is Ishmael. The prayer likely came some time after the Kaaba was built and Mecca settled, since 14:39 later mentions the gift of both Ishmael and Isaac in old age.
rows.anchor: ومن } في قوله : { من ذريتي } بمعنى بعض ، يعني إسماعيل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wādī is land between mountains; this is the valley of Mecca. ‘Without cultivation’ describes rocky land unfit for plants; dhū denotes possession and settled connection, unlike simply saying nothing grows there.
rows.anchor: والواد : الأرض بين الجبال ، وهو وادي مكة . وغير ذي زرع } صفة ، أي بواد لا يصلح للنبت لأنه حجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording parallels 39:28, ‘a Qur’an without crookedness’: the negated possessive construction means the thing is not subject to the stated quality.
rows.anchor: ولأجل هذا الاستعمال لم يقل بواد لا يزرع أولا زرع به .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Near Your Sacred House’ can be a second adjective of the valley or a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وعند بيتك } صفة ثانية لواد أو حال .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sacred House is protected from harmful human interference and harm to its people by the reverence God placed in nations’ hearts, and by the destruction of those who sought wrongdoing there; the people of the Elephant were not far off.
rows.anchor: والمحرم : الممنع من تناول الأيدي إياه بما يفسده أو يضر أهله بما جعل الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase attaches to ‘I settled’: Abraham settled them by the House so nothing would distract them from prayer there and the House would remain continually frequented.
rows.anchor: وعلق { ليقيموا } ب { أسكنت } ، أي علة الإسكان بذلك الوادي عند ذلك البيت
